title: Redwood March 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands: company metrics, product roadmap highlights, Dedicated & Private deployment updates, hiring and org changes, and open Q&A. Emphasis on production reliability, cost optimization, and go-to-market progress. Quick wins and asks for teams ahead of Q2 planning.
action_items: Ava: Share updated roadmap deck with timelines by 2026-04-01
Jordan: Run P99 latency drill for Redwood Dedicated and share results by 2026-04-08
Maya: Publish short note on KV cache improvements and known limitations by 2026-03-30
Ravi: Revise GTM playbook for Dedicated customers and circulate by 2026-04-05
next_steps: Leadership to review Q2 hiring priorities (People to schedule follow-up)
Product & Eng to sync on rollout plan for VPC Private control plane beta
Ops to prepare short incident runbook for Dedicated capacity handoffs
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 11:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom - All Hands
Attendees: Chris, Maya, Jordan, Ava, Ravi, Elena + All Employees
Agenda: Company update, Product & Roadmap, Engineering deep-dive, Hiring/org, Q&A

[00:00] Chris (CEO): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Happy to see so many faces — remote and in office. Quick housekeeping, recording is on, slides up on the right. We'll run through updates then open for Q&A. We got a packed agenda so we'll try to keep things tight.

[00:28] Chris: First, high level — Q1 closed strong. We crossed a milestone, ARR moved up and the pipeline for Dedicated is healthy. Big shout out to Revenue and Solutions teams, really good motion on mid-market.

[00:47] Ravi (Head of Revenue): Yeah, a couple of mid-market deals went live end of quarter, and we saw predictable uptick in committed capacity. There's still work on contract standardization but momentum is there.

[01:05] Maya (CTO): From infra side — we've shipped the KV cache improvements that cut cold-start token compute by about 12% in small sample. There's still perf tuning to do for long-context workloads; we're seeing some variance at high concurrency. Note: the transcript may say K-V cash in places, sorry for the auto transcribe.

[01:36] Jordan (VP Eng): We ran a P99 test last week — overall good but one of the scheduling paths under heavy load had backpressure that was suboptimal. Eng put a hotfix in, and we'll run another sweep. Also, reminder: continuous batching improvements will ship next sprint.

[02:05] Ava (Head of Product): Roadmap highlights — Dedicated autoscaling policies, better observability in Console per-route latency breakdown, and a Private beta for VPC control plane. The Private beta is limited; customers need to sign up. We'll publish details to the docs site and link from the sales playbook.

[02:37] Employee 1: Quick question on the Private beta: will the on-prem option support HSM for KMS yet?

[02:45] Maya: Short answer, not in first beta. We'll have KMS integrations for cloud KMS out of the box; HSM integration is tracked and it's targeted for a later patch. We'll share a clearer timeline soon.

[03:12] Chris: A few org notes — hiring ramp continues, we prioritized SRE, Solutions Engineering, and Product Ops this quarter. Elena will talk about ppl matters next.

[03:28] Elena (Head of People): We're opening two new SRE reqs, one Principal SE, and expanding the hiring budget for customer success. Also a reminder about the parental leave policy updates — details in the HR portal.

[03:50] Chris: On go-to-market, Ravi — quick status?

[03:55] Ravi: We're rerunning our Dedicated pricing experiments; early signs show customers are sensitive to price per token vs. predictable commit. So we're leaning into clearer cost modeling in demos — showings of batching/caching impact help conversion. One note: folks have asked for a simple benchmark sheet we can share in sales — we'll get a canonical one out.

[04:25] Jordan: On the technical front — some terminology hiccups show up in transcripts; people say Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Dedi-cated, etc — pls use the canonical branding in docs. Also small callout: quantization profiles work well with certain ops but can regress on some evals; Product will publish recommendations for workloads.

[04:55] Ava: We'll add recommended quantization profiles per model and workload to the Optimize toolkit in the next release.

[05:10] Employee 2 (chat): Is there an update on SOC 2 audit timing?

[05:15] Chris: We're on track to scope SOC 2 Type 1 in Q2 and Type 2 later in the year. Security team is aligning with compliance vendors; we'll share a timeline and FAQ for customers.

[05:34] Maya: Also we're improving audit log fidelity for Private deployments — more fields, better retention, and hooks for external SIEMs, that's in the roadmap.

[06:00] Speaker (All Hands): There's been questions about latency vs cost tradeoffs. Can you call out recommended defaults for new customers?

[06:10] Jordan: Sure — defaults are conservative: low-latency SLO uses smaller batches and higher-cost instance profiles; cost-optimized pipelines use batching and more aggressive caching. The Console will show estimated unit economics per route so AE/SEs can demo tradeoffs live.

[06:38] Ava: We're also shipping a small in-console estimator that shows token cost per request given batch size and quantization settings. It's in alpha.

[07:00] Employee 3: Any update on model catalog curation and compatibility?

[07:06] Maya: Yes — we added three curated models last month with verified perf profiles. We also added heuristics for kernel selection to pick optimal kernels for different sequence lengths; sometimes the auto selection picks suboptimal kernel on new hw — we're improving the fallback logic.

[07:35] Chris: Ok, lightning updates from teams — 60 seconds each. Infra?

[07:40] Jordan: Autoscaler improvements, jobs for better UI metrics, fixing a latent bug in the scheduler.

[07:50] Maya: Compiler/kernels: better fp16 operators for some attention paths, reduced memory for kv-cache in certain configs.

[08:05] Ava: Product Ops: updated runbooks, new canary rollout flow for model versions.

[08:20] Ravi: Sales: new playbook variant for mid-market, pilots running in EU region.

[08:35] Elena: People: new internship program kickoff in June, and manager training sessions next month.

[09:00] Q&A open floor — multiple folks ask about docs, where to find the slides, and how to volunteer for beta programs.

[09:20] Chris: For volunteers for the Private beta, please sign up on the internal form — we'll follow up from Product. Thanks for stepping up.

[09:40] Employee 4: There was a recent incident, can you recap?

[09:45] Jordan: Briefly — last week we had a regional outage due to a misconfiguration in autoscaling rules that led to throttling; impact was limited to a small subset of Dedicated customers for ~18 minutes. We rolled forward a hotfix and postmortem is in the docs. Action: lower blast radius on autoscaler changes and add a validation step.

[10:20] Chris: Thanks for the quick recovery. Please review the postmortem and suggest improvements.

[10:40] Closing — Chris: Big thanks to everyone for the sprint. Recap of top asks: product to publish roadmap deck, eng to run P99 drill and share, ops to finish incident runbook. We'll follow up in leadership sync and post notes in #all-hands channel.

[11:00] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript shows occasional mis-attributions and auto-caption artifacts (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache, Redwood Dedi-cated). Refer to meeting notes and slides for exact figures and decks.
